attempts.label: DANDI:000341
attempts.paper_title: Temporal disparity of action potentials triggered in axon initial segments and distal axons in the neocortex
attempts.entry_title: Axon initial segment and retroaxonal action potentials in layer 1 interneurons (Rozsa et al. 2023)
attempts.summary: The paper's finding that retroaxonal action potentials (RA-APs) have a lower somatic threshold and pre-AP slope than AIS-APs held up in this data, and its sag findings held in part. The share of cells with retroaxonal firing did not: 0.98 of human cells in the deposited files have RA-APs against 0.226, and the dataset does not say how its cells were selected. Nor did the reduction of retroaxonal firing by ZD7288, under epoch definitions the paper does not give, or the bleb-first arrival of RA-APs. Spontaneous RA-APs in active slices and in vivo could not be tested, as the files carry no AP labels and the paper does not give its boundary between the two classes.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Rozsa, Toth, Olah, Baka, Lakovics, Barzo and Tamas (2023) on dandiset 000341, which holds whole-cell recordings of layer 1 interneurons in human and rat slices (RAF induction, ZD7288, soma and axonal bleb, active slices with and without a layer 5 LFP) and in vivo in mice. It measures RAF patterns and prevalence, sag fractions, soma to bleb latencies, membrane potential states and LFP phase coupling, and the in vivo AP classes, rates and phase coupling.

outcomes.statement: Human layer 1 interneurons show two forms of retroaxonal firing (RAF) after induction, persistent RAF with barrages of RA-APs at high frequency (median 88 RA-APs, 13.9 Hz; duration median 17.1 s, mean 68.4 s, from 0.18 to 2809 s) and sporadic RAF with a few RA-APs at low frequency (median 8 RA-APs, 0.31 Hz).
outcomes.quote: persistent RAF showed barrages of 88 ± 1828 RA-APs with high frequencies (13.9 ± 17.3 Hz), (RAF duration: min: 0.18 s, max: 2809 s, mean: 68.4 s, and median: 17.1 ± 202.9 s); however, only a few (8 ± 6) individual RA-APs emerged at low frequencies (0.31 ± 1.5 Hz) during sporadic RAF
outcomes.notes: 307 human files with induction sweeps. Under no reading or subset are more than two of the eight values within tolerance; the measured values are those of the first reading (continuous-recording RA-APs, one epoch per cell, all cells), with none within tolerance. The best rows have two of eight (cells quiet before induction, RA-APs with the interstimulus intervals, one epoch per induction run: maximum duration 2616 s and sporadic median frequency 0.294 Hz). Both patterns occur under every reading (24 persistent and 119 sporadic epochs under the first). The reading (b) mixture fails its check (RA component slope 6.94 against 1.86 mV/ms; its size is 87879 to 2453165 APs over the five seeds), so its rows are not a reading of the paper's classes. SDs are printed beside the medians.
deviations: RA-APs by reading (c) for the main result; the dandiset carries no AP labels, and the reading (b) mixture does not recover the paper's classes in these recordings.

Induction sweeps are found from the stimulus (a sweep shorter than 1 s with one positive step of 50 to 300 ms), since the files do not mark the protocol. Some recordings use 350 ms sweeps with a 250 ms step, not the 100 ms pulses of the Methods.
Rebound APs within 0.3 s of the end of a hyperpolarizing step are left out of the RA-APs (a standard choice).
The Methods count RA-APs "during continuous recording"; the main reading uses the sweeps with no stimulus step, and the interstimulus intervals are added as a variant.

Threshold where dV/dt, taken over 50 us of the trace smoothed with a 50 us boxcar, first reaches 5 mV/ms (approximating the Methods' 10 kHz filter, so that the threshold does not depend on the sampling rate); APs with a threshold outside -80 to -10 mV or a peak above 100 mV are left out as artefacts (standard choices, added after verification round 1).

RA-APs need at most 5 pA at threshold both relative to the holding level and in absolute terms, so that APs driven by a depolarizing holding current are not RA-APs (the paper, Results: steady current was needed in some cells to reach AIS-AP threshold, and RA-APs were absent during these periods).
Each reading is also shown on the drug-free files and on the cells without spontaneous APs before induction (verifier, round 1).

outcomes.statement: RA-APs have a lower somatic threshold potential and a lower pre-AP depolarization slope than AIS-APs, during persistent and during sporadic RAF.
outcomes.quote: RA-APs during persistent RAF had lower somatic AP threshold and lower pre-AP depolarization slope values compared to AIS-APs ( 19 – 22 , 25 ). We confirmed this during sporadic RAF
outcomes.notes: Human, reading (c). Persistent cells (24): AIS-AP threshold median -44.1 mV against RA-AP -59.6 mV, slope 1.79 against 0.77 mV/ms; sporadic cells (119): -44.8 against -61.4 mV, 2.18 against 0.74 mV/ms. The paper's rule picks the Mann-Whitney U test, P printed as 0 in all four (pooled APs, 93525 to 1136274 per group). Per-cell medians agree (P = 0.0006 and 1.4e-05 in persistent cells, 1.4e-16 and 1.5e-12 in sporadic cells; RA-AP median lower in 21 to 107 of the cells). Within each human sampling rate that has both classes (10, 16.7, 25, 50 and 100 kHz) the RA-APs have the lower threshold and slope, so the difference is not a sampling-rate effect. Rat gives the same direction pooled (sporadic cells -61.6 against -41.2 mV, 0.58 against 1.67 mV/ms) and at each rate except 100 kHz, where the RA-AP threshold is the higher one (-41.69 against -42.48 mV) while the slope is lower. Reading (a) cannot be run (no labels).
deviations: The pattern of a cell is that of its single epoch of continuous-recording RA-APs (fig1ab reading (i)).

outcomes.statement: About one-fourth of tested human layer 1 interneurons (87 of 385) show RAF.
outcomes.quote: One-fourth of the tested interneurons (87 of 385 cells; Fig. 1D ) in layer 1 of the human neocortex showed RAF
outcomes.notes: Of 307 human files with induction sweeps, 301 (0.980) have at least one RA-AP under reading (c) with the interstimulus intervals and 159 (0.518) with continuous-recording RA-APs only; the drug-free files give 0.976 and 0.446, and counting the 124 cells that fire spontaneously before induction as without RAF gives 0.586 and 0.280. All are outside 0.226 +- 0.023 (87 of 385). Only variants outside the criterion fall within tolerance: at least two continuous-recording RA-APs with the cells firing before induction counted as without RAF (0.241), and a reading (b) row (0.238) whose mixture fails its check. The folder is named Human_persistent_RAF and holds 313 files, not 385 cells; the dandiset does not say how its cells were selected.
deviations: Each file is taken as one cell; no two files share a sweep fingerprint.

Subsets shown in addition (verifier, round 1): drug-free files, and cells with spontaneous APs before induction counted as without RAF or left out.

outcomes.statement: In human layer 1, RAF is predominant in neurogliaform cells (21 of 44 NGFCs) and rarer in other interneurons (9 of 90 non-NGFCs), and cannot be evoked in rosehip cells (0 of 15).
outcomes.quote: We could trigger RAF in 21 of 44 NGFCs and 9 of 90 non-NGFCs ( Fig. 1F ) and found that RAF could not be evoked in rosehip cells ( n = 15)
outcomes.notes: The human induction files carry no cell class (NGFC, non-NGFC, rosehip); their general/pharmacology table lists only drugs and ion concentrations, and no other field names a morphology. It depends on fig1d-human-raf-proportion, which ran.

outcomes.statement: About a third of tested rat layer 1 interneurons (102 of 259) show RAF.
outcomes.quote: Approximately a third of the tested cells (102 out of 259) showed RAF.
outcomes.notes: Of 118 rat files with induction sweeps, 115 (0.975) have RA-APs under reading (c) with the interstimulus intervals and 97 (0.822) with continuous-recording RA-APs only; drug-free files 0.939 and 0.788 (33 files); the lowest fraction under any reading or subset is 0.500, against 0.394 (102 of 259). The dandiset holds 132 rat files, not 259.

outcomes.statement: Rat interneurons show both sporadic RAF (frequency 1 Hz, 7 RA-APs) and tonic RAF (frequency 6.9 Hz, 100 RA-APs).
outcomes.quote: We observed both sporadic RAF (RAF frequency: 1 ± 1.8 Hz, Number of RA-AP: 7± 2.2) and tonic RAF (RAF Frequency: 6.9 ± 14 Hz, Number of RA-AP: 100 ± 241) in the rodent brain slice preparation.
outcomes.notes: Values listed for the first reading (continuous recording, one epoch per cell, all cells); no value within tolerance. No reading (c) row in any subset has a value within tolerance; one reading (b) row has one of four, and that mixture fails its check. Both patterns occur under the reading (c) rows on all cells.

outcomes.statement: In rat neocortex, RAF is found predominantly in NGFCs (22 NGFC and 10 non-NGFC RAF cells).
outcomes.quote: We repeated these experiments in the rat neocortex and confirmed the presence of both sporadic and persistent RAF in interneurons predominantly identified as NGFCs
outcomes.notes: The rat induction files carry no cell class, as for fig1f-human-raf-ngfc.

outcomes.statement: In dual soma and axonal bleb recordings of human NGFCs, AIS-APs reach the soma first and the bleb second, while RA-APs reach the bleb first, and RA-APs have lower somatic threshold and pre-AP slope.
outcomes.quote: In response to somatic depolarizing current pulses, AIS-APs were detected first on the somatic electrode and then at the axonal recording site, the order was reversed for RA-APs
outcomes.notes: The two human NGFC dual recordings are found by their celltype field (220504 and 220505 recording 2). The mixture's classes agree with the paper's description (RA component threshold -64.5 against -21.9 mV, slope 0.14 against 1.15 mV/ms; the same 74 RA-APs under all five seeds). In 220504, AIS-APs (n = 340) have a median soma-to-bleb latency of -0.20 ms at threshold and -0.14 ms at peak, so the bleb leads; RA-APs (n = 41) -0.18 ms and +0.20 ms. In 220505-2 all 62 somatic APs fall in the AIS class (+0.16 ms at threshold, +0.12 ms at peak) and there are no RA-APs. Neither cell shows AIS-APs positive and RA-APs negative. Split by the sign of the latency, which is not a reading of the criterion, the bleb-first APs of 220504 (n = 141) have the lower threshold (-27.5 against -18.3 mV) and slope (0.25 against 1.55 mV/ms). Soma and bleb sweeps of the same number start at the same time in every file. The per-file median somatic thresholds lie at -30.4 to -11.2 mV, with or without current (the RA-class APs of 220504 and 220616 have medians of -60.6 and -69.6 mV), and the voltage jump at step onset implies 26 to 57 MOhm of uncompensated resistance, so the somatic thresholds of these files are doubtful (verifier, round 1).
deviations: The bleb signal is small (peaks mostly below 0 mV), so bleb APs are not detected on their own; the bleb peak is the maximum within 3 ms of the somatic peak in the bleb sweep of the same number, and its threshold the start of the run with dV/dt at least 5 mV/ms before it (standard choices), with the smoothed dV/dt of the somatic APs.
The mixture of reading (b) is fitted to the somatic APs of the five human bleb recordings pooled.

Threshold where dV/dt, taken over 50 us of the trace smoothed with a 50 us boxcar, first reaches 5 mV/ms (approximating the Methods' 10 kHz filter, so that the threshold does not depend on the sampling rate); APs with a threshold outside -80 to -10 mV or a peak above 100 mV are left out as artefacts (standard choices, added after verification round 1).

outcomes.statement: Blocking HCN channels with ZD7288 (30 uM) reduces the duration of RAF (47.2 to 10.1 s) and the number of RA-APs (624 to 48) in human and rat layer 1 interneurons.
outcomes.quote: the duration of RAF [from 47.2 ± 36.1 to 10.1 ± 16 (s), paired sample t test, P = 0.008] and the number of RA-APs (from 624 ± 412 to 48 ± 71, paired sample t test, P = 0.007) decreased both in human ( n = 4) and in rodent ( n = 3) layer 1 interneurons

statistics.about: number of RA-APs, control against ZD7288

outcomes.notes: Seven cells (4 human, 3 rat), split at the wash-in time the files give. No reading gives both decreases at P < 0.05. One epoch per part with the interstimulus intervals: RAF duration rises from a mean of 131.6 s (median 122.8) to 359.7 s (median 422.4), paired t P = 0.017, falling in 1 of 7 cells; RA-AP count 684.6 to 596.9 (median 915 to 36), P = 0.83. Continuous recording only: duration 85.1 to 195.5 s (P = 0.25), count 658.4 to 559.6 (P = 0.80). One epoch per induction run (per-cell mean over the part's epochs): duration 59.3 to 71.6 s (P = 0.45), count 478.0 to 163.3 (P = 0.22); continuous only 29.6 to 22.7 s (P = 0.66), 463.8 to 155.7 (P = 0.23). Without the 20 uM file the picture is the same (duration 133.1 to 324.0 s, P = 0.040, rising). At most one of the four values is within tolerance under any reading. The three rat cells lose almost all RA-APs (363, 915, 180 to 13, 13, 16). Measured values are means under the first reading.
deviations: Control is the recording before DrugWashinTime1 of general/pharmacology, ZD7288 the recording after it; the paper does not say which epochs were compared, so one epoch per part and one per induction run are both shown.

Threshold where dV/dt, taken over 50 us of the trace smoothed with a 50 us boxcar, first reaches 5 mV/ms (approximating the Methods' 10 kHz filter, so that the threshold does not depend on the sampling rate); APs with a threshold outside -80 to -10 mV or a peak above 100 mV are left out as artefacts (standard choices, added after verification round 1).

outcomes.statement: ZD7288 increases input resistance (70 to 98 MOhm, P = 0.01), and hyperpolarizes the resting potential (-60 to -67 mV, P = 0.075) and decreases sag fraction (0.04 to 0.017, P = 0.057) without reaching significance.
outcomes.quote: (A) Input resistance (control: 70 ± 96 MOhm, ZD7288: 98 ± 132 MOhm, paired-sample t-test p=0.01).
outcomes.notes: Medians over 7 cells. Input resistance from the -20 pA step 146.2 MOhm in control and 141.0 under ZD7288 (means 245.5 and 252.5, paired t P = 0.78), so it does not rise significantly. Resting potential -63.6 and -63.4 mV (P = 0.39), sag fraction 0.056 and 0.047 (reading (a), -100 pA step, P = 0.54). Two of six values are within tolerance, the two resting potentials; input resistance does not rise.
deviations: Input resistance from the smallest hyperpolarizing step (-20 pA) as the criterion's standard choice; resting potential as the median pre-step baseline.

outcomes.statement: Human layer 1 interneurons have a higher somatic sag fraction than rat ones (0.15 against 0.04).
outcomes.quote: layer 1 human interneurons ( n = 358, 0.15 ± 0.29, Mann-Whitney test, P < 0.001) showed higher sag fractions compared to those in rat ( n = 254, 0.04 ± 0.4)
outcomes.notes: Reading (a) on the most hyperpolarizing step (-100 pA in nearly all cells), 312 human and 129 rat cells, human median 0.198 against rat 0.071, Mann-Whitney P = 1.5e-26, human higher; drug-free files 0.211 against 0.082, P = 8e-10. Neither median is within tolerance under any reading (b gives 0.248 and 0.076; the step nearest -90 mV gives 0.199 and 0.077 under (a)). The test holds, the medians do not.
deviations: Sag is taken from step sweeps before the first induction sweep where there are any; baseline the up to 50 ms before the step, peak the minimum after 1 ms smoothing, steady state the mean of the last 10% of the step (standard choices; the formula is not in the paper).

outcomes.statement: In both species, interneurons with RAF have smaller somatic sag fractions than those without (human 0.11 against 0.16; rat 0.02 against 0.06).
outcomes.quote: human and rat interneurons with RAF showed smaller sag fractions compared to interneurons without RAF ( Fig. 2E ; human RAF: n = 83, 0.11 ± 0.08; no-RAF: n = 275, 0.16 ± 0.16, Mann-Whitney test, P < 0.001; rat RAF: n = 97, 0.02 ± 0.07; no-RAF: n = 157, 0.06 ± 0.11, Mann-Whitney test, P < 0.001
outcomes.notes: On the tested cells (the denominator of fig1d; 6 human and 14 rat files with sag sweeps have no induction sweeps), with RAF status from the RA-APs of the continuous recording (reading (c) without the interstimulus intervals; 159 of 306 human and 95 of 115 rat cells with RAF), rat cells with RAF have the lower sag (formula (a), most hyperpolarizing step: 0.060 against 0.125, Mann-Whitney P = 0.00039; formula (b) the same P), while human cells do not (0.186 against 0.211, P = 0.12). The rat result is fragile: the step nearest -90 mV gives P = 0.0080 (formula (a)) and 0.0059 (formula (b)), and the drug-free files P = 0.0061. Counting the untested files as without RAF, as the round-2 version did, gives rat P = 2.8e-05. With the interstimulus intervals included neither species reaches P < 0.001 (rat 3 tested cells without RAF, P = 0.036; human 6, P = 0.54). No reading has more than one of the four medians within tolerance. Reading (b) gives the human difference at P < 0.001 (0.176 against 0.261), but its mixture fails its check. Measured values are on the tested cells under the assumed reading, formula (a), most hyperpolarizing step. The outcome changed from not_reproduced after verification round 1; round 2 asked for the tested cells only, and the rat P stays below 0.001.
deviations: Assumption: RAF status from the continuous-recording RA-APs. The criterion allows readings (a) to (c); with the interstimulus intervals the claim is not reproduced, with the continuous recording it is partially reproduced. The Methods count the RA-APs of an epoch "during continuous recording" ("Analysis of RAF patterns"), and the continuous recording starts once APs appear in the interstimulus interval ("Induction protocol of RAF"), so the interstimulus APs end the induction and the RA-APs counted for RAF are those after it.

Threshold where dV/dt, taken over 50 us of the trace smoothed with a 50 us boxcar, first reaches 5 mV/ms (approximating the Methods' 10 kHz filter, so that the threshold does not depend on the sampling rate); APs with a threshold outside -80 to -10 mV or a peak above 100 mV are left out as artefacts (standard choices, added after verification round 1).

RA-APs need at most 5 pA at threshold both relative to the holding level and in absolute terms, so that APs driven by a depolarizing holding current are not RA-APs (the paper, Results: steady current was needed in some cells to reach AIS-AP threshold, and RA-APs were absent during these periods).
Cells are the tested ones, those with induction sweeps, as in fig1d (verifier, round 2).

outcomes.statement: Axonal blebs show about four times the sag fraction of the soma of the same layer 1 interneurons (0.4 against 0.1), at 106 um Euclidean soma-bleb distance.
outcomes.quote: found approximately four times higher sag fractions on the axon (somatic: 0.1 ± 0.05, bleb: 0.4 ± 0.14, two-sample t test, P < 0.001)

statistics.n: 11 cells, human 2 NGFCs and 3 unidentified, rat 3 NGFCs and 3 unidentified

outcomes.notes: Reading (a), most hyperpolarizing step, each compartment from its own steps: soma median 0.024 (n = 11) against bleb 0.115 (n = 10), two-sample t P = 0.0082, paired P = 0.019; with the duplicated rat soma counted once, P = 0.011; formula (b) P = 0.027; the step nearest -90 mV gives no difference (P = 0.15). The bleb is higher with P < 0.05 but not 0.001, and neither value is within tolerance. The difference rests on step sweeps whose sag peak lies below -150 mV: without them it vanishes (soma 0.055, n = 7, against bleb 0.061, n = 6, P = 0.28). The criterion's variant, the bleb trace during a somatic step, gives bleb values near 0.9 (n = 7, P < 0.0001), which reflects a bleb deflection too small for the formula and is not taken as support. The median soma-bleb distance in the files is 106 um (9 cells, 44 to 218 um), matching the paper. One rat file has no bleb sweeps.
deviations: The bleb stimulus series (and some somatic ones) are stored in pA under a unit of amperes; they are divided by 1e12 where the values exceed 100 nA.
Shown in addition (verifier, round 1): the bleb trace during a somatic step, step sweeps with a peak below -150 mV left out, and the rat cell with two blebs counted once on the soma side.

outcomes.statement: Local application of ACSF with 5 mM K+ more than 40 um from the cell transiently induces sporadic RA-APs in human (n = 4) and rat (n = 7) layer 1 interneurons.
outcomes.quote: we injected artificial cerebrospinal fluid (ACSF) with elevated physiological K + concentration (5 mM) ( 32 ) while monitoring the membrane potential of layer 1 interneurons of >40 μm from the injection site and successfully induced sporadic RA-APs transiently in human ( n = 4) and rat ( n = 7) layer 1 interneurons
outcomes.notes: No file of the dandiset names a KCl or potassium application in its metadata (general/pharmacology, session and experiment descriptions were searched in all induction, ZD7288, bleb and active-slice files, and all general, subject and electrode fields of the in vivo files), and no folder holds the puff experiments.

outcomes.statement: In active human slices (n = 26 cells), AIS-APs occur only in depolarized up states in all 7 cells with AIS-APs, while spontaneous RA-APs, seen in 6 cells, also occur in hyperpolarized down and transition states.
outcomes.quote: AIS-APs were restricted to plateaus of depolarized membrane potential (up states) in all recorded cells with AIS-APs ( n = 7); however, when occurred (in n = 6 cells), spontaneous RA-APs were detected when the membrane potential dropped to hyperpolarized down and transition states in addition to up states
outcomes.notes: The dandiset has no AP labels, so reading (a) cannot be run, and the reading (b) mixture on the 3101 APs without current of the 26 human files gives a lower-threshold component with the steeper mean slope (3.54 against 2.18 mV/ms), the opposite of the paper's RA-APs (lower threshold and lower slope). Its classes are therefore not the paper's, and no other reading has a basis in the paper. For the record, with these classes 20 cells have AIS-APs and 12 RA-APs (expected 7 and 6); reading (i) with the mean potential before threshold puts all AIS-APs in up states in 10 of 20 cells and RA-APs in down or transition states in 6 of 12. The outcome changed from partially_reproduced after the component check the verifier asked for. The authors are asked for the AP labels (findings). The claims file's reading (b) does not ask for this check of the components; the blocking is a judgement on the classes (verifier, round 2).
deviations: The reading (b) mixture is fitted on features scaled by median and interquartile range, to a seeded draw of at most 200,000 APs; its components are printed and checked against the paper's description of RA-APs (lower threshold and lower slope).

Threshold where dV/dt, taken over 50 us of the trace smoothed with a 50 us boxcar, first reaches 5 mV/ms (approximating the Methods' 10 kHz filter, so that the threshold does not depend on the sampling rate); APs with a threshold outside -80 to -10 mV or a peak above 100 mV are left out as artefacts (standard choices, added after verification round 1).

outcomes.statement: In active human slices, membrane potential fluctuations (SD) 0 to 50 ms before AIS-APs are larger than before RA-APs (1.49 against 0.78 mV).
outcomes.quote: Membrane potential fluctuations were increased 0 to 50 ms before AIS-APs (1.49 ± 1.76 mV) compared to RA-APs (0.78 ± 1.7 mV, Mann-Whitney test, P < 0.001)
outcomes.notes: The classes are those of fig3-human-ap-states, whose mixture RA component has the steeper slope, so they are not the paper's. For the record, with these classes the SD before RA-APs is the higher one (window to threshold 5.43 against 3.18 mV, P = 2.2e-73; window to peak 7.13 against 4.97 mV, P = 2e-79). The outcome changed from partially_reproduced. The claims file's reading (b) does not ask for this check of the components; the blocking is a judgement on the classes (verifier, round 2).
deviations: The reading (b) mixture is fitted on features scaled by median and interquartile range, to a seeded draw of at most 200,000 APs; its components are printed and checked against the paper's description of RA-APs (lower threshold and lower slope).

Threshold where dV/dt, taken over 50 us of the trace smoothed with a 50 us boxcar, first reaches 5 mV/ms (approximating the Methods' 10 kHz filter, so that the threshold does not depend on the sampling rate); APs with a threshold outside -80 to -10 mV or a peak above 100 mV are left out as artefacts (standard choices, added after verification round 1).

outcomes.statement: In active rat slices, layer 5 LFP shows rhythmic low-frequency deflections at 1.1 Hz, synchronized to up states of the layer 1 interneurons.
outcomes.quote: In rat slices, somatic recordings in layer 1 interneurons ( n = 40) were accompanied by layer 5 local field potential (LFP) recordings revealing rhythmic low-frequency (1.1 ± 0.55 Hz) LFP deflections synchronized to single-cell up states
outcomes.notes: 36 rat recordings with carbachol and SCH23390 and an LFP; median spectral peak in 0.5 to 4 Hz 1.06 Hz (SD 0.48), median cycle rate of the filtered LFP 1.01 Hz (SD 0.35); both within 1.1 +- 0.11. Without the 6 recordings with extra drugs, 1.19 and 1.03 Hz. The synchronization to up states is not judged (criterion). Many spectral peaks sit at the 0.5 Hz band edge, and the cycle rate of a 0.5 to 4 Hz band-passed signal is near 1 Hz by construction, so the match is weak evidence (verifier, round 1).

outcomes.statement: In active rat slices, 13 of 40 layer 1 interneurons fire spontaneous RA-APs, and all recovered ones (n = 5) are NGFCs.
outcomes.quote: Spontaneous RA-APs were observed in 13 interneurons (all recovered cells were NGFCs, n = 5).
outcomes.notes: 36 recordings with carbachol and SCH23390 (paper 40). The mixture's RA component has the lower threshold and slope, as the paper describes (-50.8 against -44.1 mV, 1.12 against 2.79 mV/ms; 14161 to 14164 RA-APs over the five seeds). It labels RA-APs in 29 cells (at least two in 27); without the extra-drug recordings 23 of 30; without APs under a positive holding current 28 of 36. Expected 13. The mixture labels 14161 of 18779 APs as RA, while the paper counts 76 RA-APs against 534 AIS-APs (Figure 3M). The files have no cell class, so the morphology part cannot be checked. The mixture classes fail the share check added after round 2, since the RA class holds 0.754 of the APs (0.70 after the delta selection) against 0.125 in Figure 3M, and more than half of the APs in 28 of 32 recordings, so the classes are not the paper's and the numbers above do not test the claim. The outcome changed from not_reproduced to blocked after verification round 3, where the verifier agreed. The claims file's reading (b) has no share check; the blocking is a judgement on the classes.

findings.statement: Every membrane potential series gives a conversion of 1e-12 with unit volts, but the stored values are already in volts (medians near -0.065). Read with the stated conversion they are picovolts.

The stimulus series of the bleb recordings (731 sweeps) and some sweeps of other folders (52 active human, 11 ZD7288, 3 rat oscillation, and in 21 induction files) are stored in pA although their unit is amperes, giving values near 1e14 when read as stated.

No file carries AP labels (AIS-AP or RA-AP), RAF status, or the induction protocol's sweeps, so the classes and epochs the paper analyses must be rebuilt from the traces. The human and rat induction files carry no morphological cell class (NGFC, non-NGFC, rosehip), which only the bleb files record.

The local KCl application experiments (Figure 2I to 2L) are not identifiable in the dandiset, and only 2 of the 90 rat recordings without carbachol and SCH23390 (Figure S3) are in it. The in vivo folder records no anesthesia condition for any cell (Figure S5). The induction folders hold 313 human and 132 rat files against the 385 and 259 cells the paper tested.

The induction folders are named Human_persistent_RAF and Rat_persistent_RAF, and nearly all their cells fire APs without current after induction, but the paper reports RAF in a quarter to a third of tested cells. 124 of 307 human and 33 of 118 rat cells already fire spontaneous APs before induction, and 58 human and 94 rat files list drugs (including carbachol, SCH23390 and calcium changes) that the induction experiments of the paper do not mention. The dandiset does not say how its cells were selected from those the paper tested.

Sampling rates vary within and across files (5 to 200 kHz, mostly 16.7, 25, 50 and 100 kHz) against the 50 kHz of the Methods; the long gap-free sweeps of the induction files are often at 5 kHz. One bleb file (sub-20220317) has no bleb sweeps.

18 session identifiers name both an induction file and an active-slice file (2 human, 16 rat, for example ses-1611161tm-3-1-4 in Rat_persistent_RAF and in In_vitro_oscillation_Rat); the active-slice files are larger and carry an LFP. Whether these are the same recordings deposited twice is not documented, and 16 of the 18 induction files list drugs.

In the soma and bleb recordings the per-file median somatic AP thresholds lie at -30.4 to -11.2 mV with and without current, the voltage jump at the onset of depolarizing steps implies 26 to 57 MOhm of uncompensated resistance, and hyperpolarizing steps of -700 to -950 pA drive the recorded potential below -150 mV (sweep minima down to -434 mV). Bridge balance is not recorded.

The in vivo files give the genotype only inside subject/description (five values, including both 'mouse' and 'mouse-black6') and do not record the anesthesia condition; the folder holds 259 files from 149 mice against the paper's 242 cells, and some files also hold camera images ('Moovie').

disagreements.reason: I do not agree yet. The comparison does not filter on tested cells, so cells with no induction sweeps are counted as without RAF: under the assumed reading about 13 untested rat cells are in the group of 34, and under the interstimulus reading the human group of 12 has only 6 tested cells. The criterion takes RAF status as in fig1d, whose denominator is tested cells. The partial outcome rests on the rat result alone (P = 2.8e-05), already fragile (P = 0.0020 drug-free, 0.0021 at the step nearest -90 mV); rerun on tested cells only and check whether the rat P < 0.001 survives. The assumption is stated and reasonable, but part of its rationale does not hold: stopping induction when interstimulus APs appear does not imply that nearly every cell has them, and the 0.980 used there is also used as evidence of an undocumented selection.

paper_notes.statement: How AIS-APs and RA-APs were separated (a threshold and pre-AP slope boundary, per preparation or per cell), how a recording was cut into RAF epochs, and the sag fraction formula are not given. A two-component mixture on threshold and slope gives a lower-threshold component with the steeper slope in the human active slices, the in vivo recordings and the induction recordings, the opposite of the paper's RA-APs, so the claims on spontaneous human and in vivo activity cannot be tested. Could the authors give the per-AP labels or the boundary used, and the epoch definition?

entries.name: rozsa-2023
entries.title: Axon initial segment and retroaxonal action potentials in layer 1 interneurons (Rozsa et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Rozsa, Toth, Olah, Baka, Lakovics, Barzo and Tamas (2023) on dandiset 000341, which holds whole-cell recordings of layer 1 interneurons in human and rat slices (RAF induction, ZD7288, soma and axonal bleb, active slices with and without a layer 5 LFP) and in vivo in mice. It measures RAF patterns and prevalence, sag fractions, soma to bleb latencies, membrane potential states and LFP phase coupling, and the in vivo AP classes, rates and phase coupling.
